extraction.name: TextVQA
extraction.description: A dataset of 45,336 questions on 28,408 images that require reading and reasoning about text in natural everyday scenes for visual question answering.
extraction.creator: Amanpreet Singh, Vivek Natarajan, Meet Shah, Yu Jiang, Xinlei Chen, Dhruv Batra, Devi Parikh, Marcus Rohrbach
extraction.publisher: Facebook AI Research; Georgia Institute of Technology
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The dataset was collected in a three-stage crowd-sourcing pipeline. First, annotators identified and removed images without text. Second, annotators wrote 1-2 questions per image that required reading text in the image to answer, and a second different question when applicable. Third, annotators provided 10 answers for each question. Images were sampled from Open Images categories likely to contain text, using OCR-based category weighting.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Manual Human Curator, Web Scraping, Software Collection, Self-reporting
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Some images had no detectable OCR text; these cases were restricted to approximately 1.5k images and were manually verified to actually contain text. Questions marked by a majority of workers as no text in image, not a question, not requiring reading text, or unanswerable were removed.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Images from the Open Images v3 dataset, especially categories that tend to contain text such as billboard, traffic sign, and whiteboard; OCR outputs from the Rosetta OCR system were used to estimate text density and guide sampling.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Images were sampled from Open Images categories using normalized average OCR box counts as per-category weights. The dataset was split into train, validation, and test sets. Questions with majority-worker quality flags were filtered out.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Images without text were filtered out in stage one. Questions were removed if a majority of workers marked them as no text in image, not a question, not requiring reading text, or unanswerable. No image overlap was allowed between train and validation sets.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Annotators first labeled whether an image contained text. Then they wrote questions requiring reading text in the image, and optionally a second different question requiring reasoning about the text. Finally, 10 human answers were collected for each question. Quality control used additional flags and hand-crafted questions with known answers to identify bad annotators.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Each question-image pair has 10 ground truth answers. The paper reports agreement statistics: all 10 annotators agreed on the most common answer for 22.8% of questions, and 3 or more annotators agreed for 97.9% of questions.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Questions were asked by sighted humans; no further annotator demographics are provided.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: Rosetta OCR system was used to detect and recognize text in images and to estimate OCR box counts for sampling.
